Article Title: 'Save Democracy March' announced: INDIA bloc projects unity amid SIR row, targets PM Modi, Amit Shah
Article Text:
Kharge said all Opposition MPs would also march to the Election Commission on October 6

NEW DELHI: The INDIA bloc on Wednesday announced a series of nationwide protests against the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, seeking to project opposition unity amid the ongoing row over voter rolls.Addressing a press conference after the INDIA bloc meeting, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district-level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every district magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6. Kharge said the opposition had initially planned to hold the march on Wednesday but decided to organise it later with greater participation.“On October 6, all opposition MPs will march to the Election Commission. We wanted to go today itself, but we decided to call the MPs again and organise the protest properly, so we have fixed October 6 for the march,” he said.Kharge added that Rajya Sabha members and MPs from all parties, as well as those who wanted to “protect democracy in the country”, would be invited to join the march.The alliance also plans to seek an appointment with President Droupadi Murmu in the second week of October. Leaders of the opposition will submit a representation outlining what Kharge described as the difficulties they were facing and the constitutional issues involved.A fourth phase of the campaign will comprise five major rallies, with their dates and venues to be announced later.The INDIA bloc meeting also saw Kharge reiterate his criticism of the Election Commission and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He alleged that the poll panel was being influenced by the government and said the parties had agreed to fight the issue together.“From October 2 to 8, we will hold district-level 'Save Democracy' marches and stage demonstrations outside the offices of every District Magistrate. We will also make people aware of why we are undertaking this campaign,” Kharge said.Addressing the briefing, ex-Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee lashed out at the CEC and call on him to resign."He (CEC Gyanesh Kumar) must resign immediately. Let us save the democracy and make the security of the people, the voting rights... It is our constitutional rights. It is our obligation to the people. If people are not voting, if their voting are been looted and cheated, then where the country will go? So, our request...it our demand. Our forceful demand," the former Bengal CM said.The opposition has demanded a rollback of the SIR exercise, greater transparency in electoral rolls and safeguards against the exclusion of eligible voters. Kharge also called for the use of pre-SIR electoral rolls for future elections and sought prior notice, reasons and an effective appeal mechanism before legitimate voters are removed.The meeting was attended by representatives of Congress, SP, AITC, NCP(SP), SS (UBT), RJD, CPM, CPI, JKNC, JKPDP, JMM, CPI-ML, IUML, KC(M), MDMK, VCK, RSP, KC(J) and AIFB.
Article Summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge said the alliance would hold district- level “Save Democracy” marches and demonstrations outside district magistrate offices from October 2 to 8. He said all opposition MPs would march to the Election Commission on October 6.

Article Title: SIR row: 'Why does Gyanesh Kumar have lifelong immunity?' Rahul Gandhi asks, then answers
Article Text:
'PM Modi uses Gyanesh Kumar to steal elections': Rahul Gandhi on SIR irregularities

NEW DELHI: Leader of Opposition and Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Wednesday questioned the legal immunity granted to Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and alleged that Prime Minister Narendra Modi uses him to “steal elections”.In a post on X, Gandhi wrote, “Q. Why is CEC Gyanesh Kumar the only Indian with lifelong blanket legal immunity? A. Because PM Modi uses him to steal elections.”This comes as top leaders of the INDIA bloc met in New Delhi on Wednesday to finalise an action plan for a joint agitation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), with the Congress asserting that the opposition stands united to protect the Constitution from "repeated assaults" by the Modi government, including its alleged "vote chori gameplan" to remain in power.Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former party chiefs Sonia Gandhi and Rahul Gandhi, AICC general secretaries Jairam Ramesh and K C Venugopal, TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, and leaders of the SP, CPI, CPI(M), NCP(SP) and Shiv Sena (UBT), among others, attended the meeting."The INDIA janbandhan meeting just got underway. The parties participating are the Congress, Samajwadi Party, All India Trinamool Congress, NCP(SP), Shiv Sena (UBT), Rashtriya Janata Dal, CPI(M), CPI, Jammu and Kashmir National Conference, Jammu and Kashmir Peoples Democratic Party, Jharkhand Mukti Morcha, CPI-ML, IUML, Kerala Congress (M), Marumalarchi Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam, Viduthalai Chiruthaigal Katchi, RevolutionarySocialist Party, Kerala Congress (Jacob) and All India Forward Bloc," Ramesh said in a post on X."These and other Opposition parties stand united to protect the Constitution of India from repeated assaults of the Modi Government - most recently its Vote Chori gameplan through the ECI to remain in power," he added.Sources said a draft notice for a fresh motion seeking the removal of Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha was ready and would be discussed at the meeting for approval.The DMK and AAP did not attend the meeting, while SP chief Akhilesh Yadav was also absent due to the Rajya Sabha nomination process in Uttar Pradesh.The meeting comes days after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had raised objections on record at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions and orders related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), saying they had been issued without their knowledge or recommendation.Amid scrutiny over the concerns raised by the two Election Commissioners, the Election Commission said that differing views and observations were a normal part of deliberations in any institution. It also asserted that all its orders had full legal sanction and followed established statutory procedures.The last meeting of the INDIA bloc was held on June 8. Emphasising unity against the BJP, the alliance members had unanimously decided to seek the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over the NEET-CBSE row and write to the Chief Justice of India on the SIR exercise and "vote loot".
Article Summary: Top leaders of the INDIA bloc met in New Delhi on Wednesday to finalise an action plan for a joint agitation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) The Congress asserting that the opposition stands united to protect the Constitution from "repeated assaults" by the Modi government.

Article Title: Indian sailor among 5 crew killed by pirates aboard hijacked tanker off Somalia
Article Text:
Vessel was hijacked in April

Five crew members, including an Indian sailor, were killed by Somali pirates aboard a fuel tanker that was hijacked months ago off the coast of Somalia.Security forces have now regained control of the vessel.According to the Puntland Maritime Police Force (PMPF), the victims also included three Pakistani nationals and one Myanmar national."PMPF carried out a maritime operation off the coast of Dharin-baar, Bandar Beyla District, successfully rescuing the MT Honour 25 oil tanker, which had been hijacked by pirates," it said in a social media post on Tuesday.Puntland is a semi-autonomous region of Somalia.According to the PMPF, the pirates had initially offered to surrender while concealing the deaths of the crew members. It further stated that the ship was now safe and under Puntland government control. Sixteen suspected pirates were apprehended during the operation, while efforts to locate the remaining hijackers were continuing.According to the European Union’s naval force Eunavfor, the MT Honour 25 oil tanker was hijacked in April while sailing towards Somalia’s capital, Mogadishu. It was carrying around 17 crew members, most of them Pakistani nationals, along with a cargo of oil products.BBC Somali reported that the crew comprised 10 Pakistanis, four Indonesians, one Indian, one Sri Lankan and one Myanmar national.The commercial vessel, carrying 18,500 barrels of fuel bound for Mogadishu was hijacked on April 21.In a separate development, Somali pirates on Tuesday released a Togo-flagged tanker after holding it off Puntland’s Karkaar region.Nearly 30 armed pirates disembarked from the vessel and handed over all 12 crew members—eight Egyptians and four Indians—unharmed to the local community. The pirates reportedly damaged the vessel, MT Eureka, and set parts of it on fire before fleeing.The tanker had been hijacked on May 2 off Yemen’s Port of Qana while carrying 20,400 barrels of fuel. A substantial amount of its cargo was siphoned off and sold at sea during the months it was held captive. The crew members are now in the care of local residents in the Hul-Aanood area.
Article Summary: Five crew members, including an Indian sailor, were killed by Somali pirates aboard a fuel tanker that was hijacked months ago off the coast of Somalia. Security forces have now regained control of the vessel. The victims also included three Pakistani nationals and one Myanmar national.

Article Title: Delhi riots case: High court rejects bail pleas Of Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam
Article Text:
Umar Khalid, Sharjeel Imam denied bail by high court

NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court has refused to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots.Senior Advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Umar Khalid, submitted that there had been three “small changes in circumstances” since the earlier proceedings. He also referred the court to a Supreme Court judgment in support of his submissions.Pais pointed out that charges have not yet been framed in the case and, consequently, prosecution witnesses are yet to be examined. The court also noted that the charges were yet to be framed.Pais further submitted that a Special Leave Petition (SLP) is pending before the Supreme Court and that the trial court has indicated it would await the Supreme Court’s order. He then continued his submissions by referring to the Supreme Court judgment.Khalid and Imam had approached the Delhi High Court earlier this year after their bail applications were dismissed by the trial court for the third time on July 4. Imam was arrested in the case on August 25, 2020, while Khalid was arrested on September 13, 2020.The Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots, PTI reported.The police argued that they could not seek bail on parity with other co-accused, stating that the Supreme Court had earlier categorised them as being part of the “command authority” and held that their “risk profiles” justified “continuing detention”.The police also argued that the present bail pleas were in the teeth of the Supreme Court’s January 5 order, which directed them to seek release only after the examination of protected witnesses was completed or after one year, whichever was earlier.On July 4, the trial court rejected Khalid’s bail application, saying it had “no option but to follow” the Supreme Court’s January 5 order and could therefore neither entertain the plea nor grant him relief.On September 2, 2025, a Delhi High Court division bench denied bail to Khalid and Imam. The Supreme Court upheld the verdict on January 5 but granted relief to co-accused Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justice Aravind Kumar and Justice NV Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the UAPA.On May 22, the Supreme Court granted six months’ interim bail to co-accused Abdul Khalid Saifi and Tasleem Ahmad, while referring to a larger bench the issue of prolonged incarceration of undertrials under the UAPA due to the stringent conditions for granting bail.
Article Summary: Delhi High Court refuses to grant bail to Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam in the UAPA case related to the 2020 Delhi riots. Delhi Police has opposed their bail pleas in the high court, asserting that the two were “masterminds” of the riots.

Article Title: NEET-UG to shift online? Centre works on nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy
Article Text:
NEET-UG may shift online as Centre develops nationwide CBT infrastructure strategy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy to enable the transition of NEET from its current pen-and-paper format to an online examination, officials said.While NEET has so far been conducted in pen-and-paper mode, the National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts several other examinations, including JEE-Main, Common University Entrance Test (CUET)-UG and PG, UGC-NET and CSIR UGC-NET, in computer-based mode.Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode."A national examination-grade Computer-Based Testing infrastructure strategy is being formulated to close the geographic gap in test-centre availability, standardise centre-level examination-grade specifications and to permit the migration to CBT from the pen-and-paper mode examinations. The strategy is under active consideration based on a multi-model sourcing architecture," a senior Ministry of Education official was quoted as saying by PTI.The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA), the nodal autonomous body responsible for conducting NEET-UG and other entrance examinations for higher educational institutions."The possible migration of NEET (UG) from the pen-and-paper mode to CBT, including the design of the transition, the sequencing, the infrastructure prerequisites, and the equity implications for rural, women and low-connectivity-district candidates, is being worked upon.However, the recommendations of the High-Level Task Force on exam reforms in structured consultation and concurrence of the Health Ministry and National Medical Commission, are awaited," the official said.Following the NEET paper leak earlier this year, the Centre announced that the medical entrance examination would be conducted in Computer-Based Test (CBT) mode from next year.Officials aware of the development said the plan is under active consideration, but a final decision will be taken only after the report of the Nandan Nilekani-led task force set up to overhaul India’s public examination system is received.The leak of the NEET-UG medical entrance examination paper earlier this year triggered nationwide student protests and led to the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.A day after Pradhan’s resignation, Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced the formation of a high-powered task force headed by Infosys co-founder Nandan Nilekani to recommend reforms aimed at making the examination system leakproof.The panel has yet to submit its report.The National Eligibility Entrance Test (NEET)-UG is the country’s largest undergraduate entrance examination, with nearly 25 lakh candidates appearing for the crucial test.The National Testing Agency (NTA) conducts NEET every year for admission to medical colleges. A total of 1,08,000 seats are available for the MBBS course, of which approximately 56,000 are in government hospitals and about 52,000 in private colleges. NEET results are also used for admissions to undergraduate courses in Dentistry, Ayurveda, Unani and Siddha.
Article Summary: The ministry of education is developing a nationwide Computer-Based Testing (CBT) infrastructure strategy. Once the infrastructure strategy is in place, the plan is to shift all entrance examinations to the online mode. The move comes amid an ongoing overhaul of the National Testing Agency (NTA)

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Wednesday drew a parallel between the British policy of “divide and rule” and what it described as the Congress ’ “divide Hindus for Muslim rule” approach, while targeting Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy over his remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Shiva.BJP MP and party spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi, speaking at a press conference at the BJP headquarters in New Delhi, said, “The Britishers used the concept of divide and rule... Congress’ approach is to divide Hindus for Muslim rule.”To reinforce his argument, Trivedi claimed that Congress MP and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi had “deliberately chosen” a Muslim-majority constituency. He was referring to Rahul Gandhi’s former constituency of Wayanad in Keralam, a seat where Muslims account for more than 40% of the electorate and form the majority.The Congress leader currently represents Uttar Pradesh’s Raebareli constituency in the Lok Sabha.The controversy stems from Revanth Reddy’s remarks at a media conclave in New Delhi on September 28.Responding to a question about the Congress’ weak presence in North India, Reddy said, “We are Dravidians. People here (north) are Aryans. We are devotees of Shiva. These are devotees of Lord Ram. BJP stole Ram. It's an emotion.It's a sentiment. Why Modi ji does not say Har Har Mahadev. Have BJP people ever said Har Har Mahadev on a stage. They say only Jai Sri Ram. When we say Har Har Mahadev, they don't like it.”“Shiva is the God of the poor, Ram is the God of the rich and the BJP is a party of the rich,” he added.The remarks predictably drew a sharp response from the BJP, while the Congress defended Reddy, saying that Lord Ram “looks rich” and Lord Shiva “physically looks poor.”"Why should he (CM Revanth Reddy) apologise? I'm defending Revanth Reddy. Look-wise, Lord Ram wears a lot of ornaments. He looks rich, whereas Lord Shiva, with no clothes, physically looks poor. That is the difference. But we have affection for both the Gods, we pray to them, and we wish that both the Gods bless us," Telangana Congress president Mahesh Kumar Goud said.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy made controversial remarks on Lord Ram and Lord Shiva. Reddy said, “We are Dravidians. People here (north) are Aryans. We are devotees of Shiva.” The remarks predictably drew a sharp response from the BJP, while the Congress defended Reddy.

NEW DELHI: India produced another strong medal haul at the Asian Games 2026 on Monday, winning eight medals across athletics, shooting and kurash. However, the impressive collection did not bring any change in the overall standings, with India remaining 12th as the country continued to wait for another gold medal.India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze.'The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh, while Rohit Yadav, Parul Chaudhary, Vithya Ramraj and Pincky Balhara won bronze.India's strongest showing came in the men's javelin, where Yashvir and Rohit produced a double podium finish in the absence of defending champion Neeraj Chopra.Yashvir recorded a personal best of 85.72m for silver, while Rohit won bronze with 84.35m. Sri Lanka's Rumesh Pathirage claimed gold with 88.55m.Sreeshankar also won silver in the men's long jump with 8.07m despite an injury forcing him to abandon his final two attempts. China's Yuhao Shi took gold with 8.17m.Gulveer added his second silver of the Games with a personal best of 3:36.72 in the men's 1500m, having earlier finished runner-up in the 10,000m.Parul Chaudhary won bronze in the women's 5000m with 15:14.61, adding to the bronze she had claimed in the 3000m steeplechase.Vithya Ramraj also took bronze in the women's 400m hurdles with a personal best of 54.75 seconds.Esha Singh secured silver in the women's 25m pistol after finishing with 38 hits, the same score as China's Xiao Jiaruixuan, who won the gold after the shoot-off.Pincky Balhara added bronze in the women's -78kg kurash category, losing 0-5 to South Korea's Sumin Mo in the semifinals.Despite the eight medals, India's gold tally remained at four, a crucial factor in the standings as countries are ranked by gold medals first.China led with 132 golds, followed by Japan with 41, South Korea with 21 and Uzbekistan with 12. India remained 12th with 45 medals, highlighting how a large haul of silver and bronze medals has yet to translate into a significant rise in the standings.
Article Summary: India added four silver and four bronze medals during the day but could not increase its gold tally. After Day 9, India stood at 45 medals — four gold, 20 silver and 21 bronze. The eight-medal haul included silver medals for Yashvir Singh, Murali Sreeshankar, Gulveer Singh and Esha Singh.

Article Title: Watch: Massive fire destroys 8 houses, several cowsheds in J&K's Kishtwar

NEW DELHI: A fire that broke out shortly after midnight reduced at least eight houses and several cowsheds to ashes in a remote village in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district.The fire erupted in a house in Mungli village in the Warwan area and spread rapidly to neighbouring structures. With residents struggling to contain it, earth movers were used to pull down parts of the affected houses and create a gap to prevent the flames from spreading further.No human casualties were reported in the blaze but reporting suggests that there have been livestock casualties.The exact extent of the livestock loss, however, could not be ascertained as a detailed assessment was not possible during the night, as reported by news agency PTI.The absence of a fire station in Warwan meant fire tenders had to be summoned from Kokernag in south Kashmir's Anantnag district. The firefighting operation continued for several hours before the blaze was brought under control around 4 am.Officials said the site was being monitored as some areas were still smouldering.The cause of the blaze was also not immediately known.The local administration has begun assessing the damage and the relief needed by affected families.A relief vehicle is also being arranged from the district headquarters, officials said.The incident comes as authorities regularly warn residents in the remote Warwan region about the risk of fires during winter. Families commonly stockpile dry grass and fodder for their livestock during the season, and officials have advised them to keep such material away from homes and other residential structures.Similar precautions have also been communicated through government and religious institutions in the area.
Article Summary: A fire that broke out shortly after midnight reduced at least eight houses and several cowsheds to ashes in a remote village in Jammu and Kashmir's Kishtwar district. No human casualties were reported in the blaze but reporting suggests that there have been livestock casualties.

NEW DELHI: The Indian Coast Guard , in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS), seized approximately 526 kg of narcotics from an Iranian dhow in the Arabian Sea west of Lakshadweep, officials said.The Coast Guard said five Pakistani nationals operating the vessel were also detained during the operation carried out near Lakshadweep on September 25, as reported by news agency PTI.The drugs, valued at over Rs 3,000 crore in the international market, were seized after the vessel was intercepted during the operation.The Coast Guard conducted coordinated sea-air surveillance to track the suspicious vessel before launching a hot pursuit and boarding the dhow.The operation was carried out in coordination with the Gujarat Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) to intercept the vessel. The seized contraband comprised heroin and methamphetamine, while five Pakistani nationals operating the dhow were also apprehended.The dhow, its crew and the seized drugs were escorted to Mumbai under armed security for joint interrogation and further legal proceedings.The operation was part of coordinated efforts by the Coast Guard and Gujarat ATS to detect and disrupt suspected transnational maritime drug-smuggling networks.The seizure comes as Indian maritime and law enforcement agencies continue efforts to prevent narcotics from being smuggled through sea routes. The Coast Guard has previously conducted joint operations with Gujarat ATS and other agencies to intercept vessels suspected of carrying illegal drugs.In April 2025, the Coast Guard, along with Gujarat ATS, seized 307.5 kg of narcotics off the Gujarat coast, according to the Coast Guard's official record of interdiction cases.Several drug-interdiction operations have been conducted along maritime routes in the Arabian Sea, with agencies relying on intelligence inputs, vessel surveillance and coordination between maritime and land-based enforcement units to identify suspected consignments.The Coast Guard said the latest operation underlined its efforts to strengthen maritime surveillance and prevent illicit activities in India's maritime zones. The seized drugs and apprehended crew were brought to Mumbai for further investigation and legal action.
Article Summary: Indian Coast Guard intercepts Iranian dhow, seizes 526 kg narcotics worth over Rs 3,000cr. The seized contraband comprised heroin and methamphetamine. Five Pakistani nationals operating the dhow were also apprehended. The seizure comes as Indian maritime and law enforcement agencies continue efforts to prevent narcotics from being smuggled.

Article Title: Meet Dhanraj Parimal, corporate honcho & Samajwadi Party's surprise candidate for Rajya Sabha
Article Text:
Samajwadi Party picks Ramgopal Yadav, Dhanraj Nathwani for Rajya Sabha from UP

LUCKNOW: Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is Samajwadi Party's 'surprise' candidate for the Rajya Sabha polls along with party's secretary general Prof Ram Gopal Yadav. Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is the Group President of Reliance Industries and considered to be very close to the Ambani family. He is also a sports administrator. The two will file their nomination papers in the presence of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav at 11 am.Recently, Akhilesh Yadav, while responding to a media query on probable candidates for Rajya Sabha had said that this time there will be a surprise candidate from SP. On Wednesday morning the party declared Nathwani's name as the second confirmed candidate of the party on SP's official X account.A founding member of SP and party founder Mulayam Singh Yadav's chief political strategist, Ram Gopal Yadav has been in the Rajya Sabha continuously since 2004. He has stood with Akhilesh through all the thick and thin and sided with him during the battle for supremacy within the Yadav clan in the run-up to 2017 assembly polls.As per the math in place, SP has INDIA bloc MLAs to see through two of its candidates in Rajya Sabha and will need some outside MLAs for any third candidate.As Group President at Reliance Industries Limited (RIL), Dhanraj looks after Corporate Affairs, Finance, HR, and CSR. He oversees the operations of Reliance's Jamnagar and Vadodara manufacturing divisions in Gujarat.Dhanraj is also a Director in other Reliance Group entities including Reliance New Energy Limited.He was unanimously elected as the President of Gujarat Cricket Association (GCA) in 2022 succeeding Union Home Minister Amit Shah and also is also the President of Gujarat State Football Association.Dhanraj also happens to be the Vice-President of the administrative committee of the famous Dwarkadhis Temple and has directed the famous mega-musical show 'Rajadhiraj: Love.' based on the life journey of Lord Krishna.With a Bachelor's Degree in International Business from Regent Business School (London), Dhanraj is an animal lover actively involved in wildlife conservation. He has been associated with campaigns for conservation of Gir lions.
Article Summary: Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani is the Group President of Reliance Industries and considered to be very close to the Ambani family. The two will file their nomination papers in the presence of SP chief Akhilesh Yadav at 11 am.

Article Text:

What is the textbook row about?

NEW DELHI: Students and members of farmers' and youth organisations staged protests in Bhubaneswar on Wednesday as a 12-hour statewide Odisha bandh was observed over alleged errors in school textbooks and a demand for the resignation of school and mass education minister Nityananda Gond.Members of the Naba Nirman Krushak Sangathan (NNKS) and Nabnirman Yuva Chhatra Sangathan (NYCS) blocked a national highway at Baramunda bus stand and torched tyres during the protest. Visuals from the protest showed demonstrators occupying the road as traffic movement was disrupted.The NNKS has called the bandh over what it described as large-scale errors in textbooks used in government schools. The organisation has been holding a relay hunger strike since August 20 and said the agitation would remain peaceful. NNKS national coordinator Akshay Kumar has been on hunger strike in Bhubaneswar since September 6.Speaking to ANI, M D Manwar Ali, state convenor of the Nabnirman Yuva Chhatra Sangathan, said the bandh had begun across the state."Right now, the Odisha Bandh is happening in Bhubaneswar at Baramunda. On that side is Hanspal, on this side is Uttara. Accordingly, across Odisha—whether West Odisha, East Odisha, or South Odisha—you will see picketing has started everywhere."The NNKS claimed that more than 1,700 errors had been identified in newly published school textbooks, while NYCS alleged that the number was more than 2,000 in books for Classes 1 to 8. Among the examples cited were a reference to the Niyamgiri Hills as being in Jharkhand and a picture of the Karnataka assembly being used instead of the Odisha assembly. The organisations also alleged that scientist Isaac Newton was described as a pilot.Ali alleged irregularities in the textbook preparation process and claimed corruption worth Rs 380 crore. "Demanding the resignation of Odisha’s Mass Education Minister Nityananda Gond, we have called for an Odisha Bandh today. We request everyone to support this call. In Odisha, for children's school textbooks from Class 1 to Class 8, there are more than 2,000 errors and a corruption of ?380 crore has taken place," he said.The organisations said they had received no response from the government despite their protests. "Therefore, today our demand is that Odisha’s Mass Education Minister must resign. Today marks 42 days of our protest. Our organisation’s founder Akshaya Ji has been on protest for 25 days, and today is my 18th day. We sat there at the protest venue (Dharna Sthal), but no representative from the government came to talk or ask for his resignation.That’s why we gave the call for the Odisha Bandh," Ali said.The state Home Department alerted district collectors ahead of the bandh and directed them to strengthen security at sensitive locations and ensure essential services continued. In Bhubaneswar, police deployed 10 platoons of force and 15 officers at designated locations.
Article Summary: The NNKS has called the bandh over what it described as large-scale errors in textbooks used in government schools. The organisation has been holding a relay hunger strike since August 20 and said the agitation would remain peaceful. The organisations said they had received no response from the government despite their protests.

Article Title: As US cozies up to Pakistan, India warns it could impact ties
Article Text:
India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.

S Jaishankar: Delay in reaching trade deal created bumps in relationship

NEW YORK/ NEW DELHI: Amid growing US-Pakistan bonhomie, external affairs minister S Jaishankar warned that a lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties.Flagging issues pertaining to each other’s sensitivities, the minister said that terrorism was of particular importance to India.“There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” Jaishankar said, without naming Pakistan.“Now, if something which matters so deeply to us, there isn’t enough understanding or appreciation or empathy of that, I think that creates a problem too. That you know if... one of my primary concerns is not fully appreciated by my partner, then clearly there is an impact of that on the relationship,” he said, alluding to India-US ties.Jaishankar’s remarks followed US President Donald Trump’s sharing on social media a video clip of Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif’s UNGA speech where he thanked the president for his “timely intervention” to end India’s Op Sindoor. Jaishankar was speaking at the Asia Society Policy Institute where he was asked about the state of the bilateral relationship amid differences over trade and tariffs.The minister said that the trade deal both sides are finalising can improve relations, but added that the period it took to reach the understanding created bumps in the relationship.Bear in mind, India is a society of small producers, small agriculture producers, small factories. Apart from the per capita gap between India and the US, the nature of production, nature of society is very different,” he said.“A trade negotiation required a certain amount of ... patience and detailing to see it through… The expectation that it could rapidly move forward, I think, was tested against a ground reality which was much more complex,” added the minister.Jaishankar said that “today, we have reached a situation where there is more or less an understanding on the trade agreement”.India and the US had in Feb announced the finalisation of the framework for the first phase of the bilateral trade agreement. However, changes in the US tariff landscape have led to further negotiations on the agreement.The two sides have since continued negotiations on their bilateral trade agreement amid the changes in the US tariff regime. Jaishankar, alluding to comments by commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal, said the issue now was what had changed on the American side and how the new Section 301 process would affect the agreement. “The 301 process is still in the works, it’s still unfolding. So the issue for us is at what point do you close out an agreement which is very, very far advanced,” Jaishankar said.“But the period that it took to reach it, that did create bumps last year for the relationship. So presumably, if that agreement is closed out, that would be one point which would contribute to a better relationship,” he said.
Article Summary: S Jaishankar: A lack of understanding about India’s concerns over cross-border terrorism will affect India-US bilateral ties. “There are very few countries which have been subjected to the kind of terrorism that we have from a neighbour as part of a deliberate, conscious policy over many, many decades,” he said.

One of the enduring memories of the Mamata Banerjee era in West Bengal will be the elaborate Durga Puja carnival, where handpicked(marquee pujas) would parade along Red Road with tableaux before the CM and other dignitaries in an almost Republic Day-esque procession. It would often end with Mamata Banerjee doing an impromptu jig with the crème de la crème of the Bengali film industry.The carnival has been scrapped. Instead, a pre-Puja event will be held at the iconic Eden Gardens on Mahalaya, October 10, which Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend. These and many other changes are expected as West Bengal counts down to the homecoming of the Goddess.This year marks a significant break in Bengal's politics. The BJP government took office on May 9, making this its first Durga Puja in power in the state. And some changes are already in motion. Beyond the cosmetic, is Bengal's intrinsic style of celebrating Durga Puja going to change?The number of pujas continues to grow. As of September 24, 2,318 Durga Pujas had already registered on Kolkata's Sahaj single-window permission portal, including 270 new applicants, with more applications still expected. In 2025, the final tally of 2,936 applications was the highest ever. Across Bengal, the state power department expects the number of community pujas to cross 65,000 this year, an estimate based partly on demand for temporary electricity connections.The, or community-puja, tradition in Bengal is generally traced to late-18th-century Guptipara, although historians differ over the precise year and even whether the earliest community celebration there was Durga Puja or Jagaddhatri Puja. The wordis generally traced to, or "twelve friends". From the patronage of zamindars to that of influential political leaders, Durga Puja's format has constantly changed, though it remains the cornerstone of Bengal's annual cultural calendar.From, where the divine family is presented within a single frame, to multi-part installations; from, or traditional-style idols, to theme pujas; fromto idols made from unconventional materials, creative people have continually found new ways to express their love and reverence for Goddess Durga.In the run-up to Mahalaya, Kumartuli, north Kolkata's famous idol-making quarter, draws growing crowds of photographers, selfie-seekers and curious visitors into its narrow lanes. The adjoining Kumartuli Ghat is now adding another attraction. A Rs 10-crore redevelopment of a 300-metre stretch of the Hooghly riverfront, with viewing areas, walkways and improved public facilities, is expected to add to the draw.The most visible change this year is in the patronage of Durga Pujas. For years, the names of influential Trinamool leaders were virtually interchangeable with those of Kolkata's marquee pujas. There was Sujit Bose's Sreebhumi, Arup Biswas's Suruchi, Firhad Hakim's Chetla Agrani and Partha Chatterjee's Naktala Udayan Sangha, among others.Along with these, many up-and-coming political leaders ensured that relatively unknown Durga pandals shot to fame with innovative themes. Often, hosting a large-scale Durga Puja became a proxy for growing political clout.That competition for spectacle and social ownership, however, long predates contemporary party politics. Kaliprasanna Sinha's 19th-century Hutom Pyanchar Naksha used Durga Puja to lampoon Calcutta's babu culture, its display, extravagance and social pretensions.At Sreebhumi Sporting Club, the extravaganza that became synonymous with former Trinamool minister Sujit Bose is being prepared by a new committee. BJP leader Kanak Debnath has become president, with the organisers promising to retain the puja's grandeur while ending prolonged road blockades.At Suruchi Sangha, for years associated with Arup Biswas and his brother Swarup, BJP MLA Sourav Sikdar is now secretary. Suruchi's new committee has replaced the Biswas brothers, although the transition was accompanied by protests from residents. At Tala Prattoy, which has been delivering extremely eye-catching themes over the last few years, much of the previous organising set-up has changed, with Sushanta Shibani Pal handling this year's theme.The organisational change is extending beyond individual clubs. A new statewide coordination platform, Paschim Banga Durga Puja Samannay Samiti, or West Bengal Durga Puja Coordination Committee, is taking shape, with Kartik Maharaj as chairman and BJP MLA Rudranil Ghosh as chief adviser. It could emerge as an alternative pole to the established Forum for Durgotsab, which represents hundreds of committees.The churn has reached venues old and new. Known for its elaborate Christmas and New Year celebrations, Park Street will host a Durga Puja at Allen Park for the first time this year. Without missing a beat, Kolkata Sanatani Sangha, fronted by BJP leader Shankudeb Panda, will be organising it.At Mohammad Ali Park, competing committees put up banners under different names after BJP councillor Meena Devi Purohit proposed renaming the historic venue Mahabali Park. The iconic Bagbazar Puja, meanwhile, landed in trouble over a deadlocked committee election before the courts sorted it out.The financial machinery behind Durga Puja is also being recalibrated. The Mamata Banerjee government introduced annual assistance to puja committees at Rs 10,000 in 2018 and increased it over the years to Rs 1.1 lakh in 2025. The new BJP government has announced Rs 1 lakh for 2026, while chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has appealed to big-budget organisers to leave the assistance for smaller celebrations that need it.During TMC rule, BJP leader Sajal Ghosh's Santosh Mitra Square was something of a 'rebel' puja, refusing to take grants. With power having changed hands and TMC virtually disintegrating, there are no such rebel pujas this time, at least publicly.Several prominent committees have agreed to forgo the grant, in line with the government's appeal. The BJP government has also asked electricity suppliers to provide free power to organisers; under the previous government, the waiver in 2025 was 80%.In Birbhum, BJP district president Uday Shankar Banerjee told puja committees that clubs taking the 2026 government grant must display the chief minister's photograph or face action, a claim promptly shot down by minister Dilip Ghosh.It is perhaps on food that the focus will be most intense.In late August, Swami Nirgunananda, a member of the VHP's central advisory council, suggested that non-vegetarian food should be kept away from the immediate puja space, while acknowledging that Bengal's Durga Puja has never been exclusively vegetarian. VHP leaders subsequently clarified that there was no official or binding directive banning non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja.Days later, religious preacher Dhirendra Krishna Shastri, popularly known as Bageshwar Baba, went considerably further. He criticised the consumption of non-vegetarian food during Durga Puja, describing those who did so as, or hypocrites.The remarks provoked criticism, including from within the BJP. State party president Samik Bhattacharya defended Bengal's food traditions, while Adhikari subsequently visited Kalighat temple and consumed traditional prasad that included fried fish, fish head and basanti pulao. At Suruchi Sangha, where BJP MLA Sourav Sikdar is now secretary, organisers have said mutton and hilsa will continue to be served at the Maha Navami feast. Many housing societies where community Durga Pujas take place have also affirmed that their Puja feasts aren't going to change and will remain largely non-vegetarian, barring Maha Ashtami.In large parts of north India, abstaining from meat during Navratri is commonplace. Critics of the BJP have expressed concern that such a food culture could gradually be pushed on Bengal. There is no evidence of any government plan to impose such a restriction. But the effect could be subtler than a formal ban.Some organisers are already drawing a firmer boundary around the immediate sacred space. Thakurpukur SB Park and Chaltabagan have announced restrictions on visitors entering while eating, while the new Allen Park puja will have no food stalls inside the park, TOI has reported previously.There is a perception that, at many pandals, egg-roll stalls and other non-vegetarian food outlets will be stationed farther away from the main arena where the Goddess will be placed.Theme pujas have not been barred, but organisers have been asked to ensure that idols and themes do not hurt religious sentiments or undermine what the new government describes as Sanatani traditions. That has prompted some artists and organisers to tread more cautiously.However, social and experimental subjects continue this year too, including themes around care workers, gender identity and ecology. What is changing is the political vocabulary surrounding them. At the same time, several high-profile pujas this year are invoking patriotism, nationalism and Hindu cultural identity.There is no official census separating theme pujas from traditional ones.Santosh Mitra Square, whose committee is headed by BJP MLA Sajal Ghosh, has chosen. New Town Sanatani Durga Puja, whose leadership includes chief ministerial adviser Subrata Gupta and Kartik Maharaj, is exploring what its organisers describe as the relationship between ancient Indian traditions and modern science.The use of Goddess Durga as a political or nationalist metaphor is hardly new. In Bankimchandra Chattopadhyay's(My Durga Puja), included in, an opium-addled Kamalakanta looks at the Durga image on Saptami and eventually sees in her Bengal itself (, Mother Bengal), invoking the Goddess as an image of collective strength and awakening.Nazrul would later take the idea in another direction. In his Durga and Agomoni compositions, the rebel poet repeatedly invoked the Goddess as Shakti, or living power, rather than merely an image of clay. His 1922 poemused Durga's arrival as an anti-colonial metaphor so explicitly that the British prosecuted him for sedition The VHP's Nirgunananda, though, has argued for a more explicitly religious ownership of the festival. At an August meeting with Puja organisers, he rejected the formulation that "religion belongs to individuals, but festivals belong to everyone", arguing instead that festivals primarily belong to followers of the faith, while people of other religions were welcome to visit.That marks a clear difference in outlook, which may well become one of the faultlines around Bengal's Durga Puja celebrations.Pandal-hopping has also traditionally been an easy way to get a crash course in political history.The Left Front's stalls, where thewould be stationed selling books on, or Marxist philosophy, were hard to miss. Seeing them, the TMC also started its Jago Bangla stalls, though Didi, a skilled politician, never quite got the stamp of approval from Bengalis for her literary exploits.This year, though, the Left may face problems putting up some of those stalls.The name, synonymous with Durga Puja, is facing questions. Chief minister Suvendu Adhikari has asked committees not to accommodate CPI(M) bookstalls that describe the festival as "Sharadotsav" instead of "Durga Puja", arguing that the terminology dilutes its religious identity.Interestingly, Rabindranath Tagore wrote, a play celebrating the autumn season, way back in 1908, a point also raised by Left leaders in response to the controversy. A puja committee at Kamardanga in Tangra has gone further, announcing that it will not allow stalls run by CPI(M), DYFI, SUCI or other Left-wing organisations at its celebration. The committee has appealed to other organisers to follow suit, while CPI(M) has criticised the move.The Red Road immersion carnival, first held under Mamata Banerjee's government in 2016, has been discontinued. In its place comes a grand Mahalaya celebration at Eden Gardens on October 10, 2026, one week before Maha Shashthi on October 17. The programme is expected to feature traditional performers, thousands of dhakis, fireworks and a drone show. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to attend and virtually inaugurate prominent Kolkata pujas from the programme. The Eden Gardens presentation aims to recreate important events and rituals associated with Durga Puja.Mahalaya holds a very special significance. Beyond, the ritual offering to one's ancestors, Birendra Krishna Bhadra's recitation in theradio programme, which became associated with Mahalaya from the 1930s, has itself become a ritual. Hosting such a gala event on that day gives the new government a prominent ceremonial role at the opening of Bengal's Puja season.There are changes for ordinary pandal-hoppers too. The new government has said Puja pandals will not be allowed to be inaugurated before Mahalaya. Maha Ashtami will be a dry day, with liquor sales prohibited. DJs have been banned during Puja celebrations and immersion processions, while organisers have been instructed to avoid prolonged road blockades and complete immersions within the prescribed period.Even the appearance of Kolkata Police's crowd-management volunteers is set to change, with police floating a tender for orange T-shirts and caps to replace the familiar white-and-blue attire.There is not much clarity yet about how active the TMC will be during Durga Puja. But one thing Kolkata will surely be revisiting through reels is Mamata Banerjee's one-liners and gestures, from her suggestion that, the tall white kans grass associated with the Bengali autumn, could be used as stuffing for pillows to her symbolicSo will Bengal's intrinsic style of celebrating Puja change? The answer may lie in how varied that style has always been.There has never been one compulsory Bengali Puja menu, or even one compulsory visual grammar. Mahendranath Datta, the younger brother of Swami Vivekananda, recorded striking differences between Durga images in Shakta and Vaishnava households . In Shakta homes, he wrote, Durga's lion had the conventional lion's face; in Gosain or Vaishnava homes, the lion had a horse-like face, apparently marking a distinction between the two traditions. On food too, practices differed. At Brahmin homes, guests could be served rice, five vegetable dishes, curd and payesh; in Shakta Brahmin households, he noted, fish was also permitted, while Kayastha homes served luchi.The traditions that have survived in Bengal's old family pujas are equally difficult to squeeze into a single dietary rule. The Sabarna Roy Chowdhury family continues to offer katla as Nabami bhog.At Chorbagan Chatterjee Bari, fish is offered during the Puja days. At the Janbazar home of Rani Rashmoni's descendants, on the other hand, the Goddess receives vegetarian bhog even as non-vegetarian food is served to guests, reported TOI previously.There is no quick primer on how to be Sanatani across Bengal's myriad Durga Puja traditions. The pandals may change hands, and the colour of uniforms may change. But beneath the contest for ownership lies a diversity of practice too old and too deep-rooted.Perhaps the more things change, the more they stay the same.
Article Summary: This year marks a significant break in Bengal's politics. The BJP government took office on May 9, making this its first Durga Puja in power in the state. The carnival has been scrapped. Instead, a pre-Puja event will be held at the iconic Eden Gardens on Mahalaya.

Article Title: Pakistan airspace closed, India eyes China skies
Article Text:
Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.

NEW DELHI: India is trying to work out a “Pakistan bypass” with China for its domestic airlines as the latest closure since April 2025 has made routes between Delhi and West unviable due to longer detours amid soaring oil prices. India is in talks with China to make the Hotan route in Xinjiang available to its airlines.The Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with Air India and IndiGo doing feasibility studies. AI’s Boeing 777s, B787s and Airbus A350s can take the route. IndiGo can do so after it starts getting A350s.“We are exploring alternate airspaces and Hotan is under discussion. Diplomatic-level talks are underway. We are strongly pushing for Hotan. We are asking Indian airlines to launch more international flights from other parts of India (where western routes are not impacted by Pak airspace closure) like the south and improve connectivity from there,” aviation minister Ram Mohan Naidu said on the sidelines of Routes Asia 2027 Tuesday.India is keen on a Pakistan bypass as international travel is growing at about 5% over the past decade, while airlines’ growth plans are hit by the neighbour’s airspace closures.To be sure, India also reciprocally closes its airspace for Pak airlines but their operations are mainly to the West.Air India, which lost Rs 4,000 crore due to Pakistan airspace closure in a year, had made a presentation on the Hotan waypoint route.Some AI wide body aircraft have additional oxygen storage, allowing them more time to step descend to 14,000 feet and then 10,000 feet in case of single engine failure or cabin de-pressurisation while flying out of the region.This is the second time in five years that Air India has found an alternate way around an airspace closure. Before Aug 2021, AI flights used the Pakistan-Afghanistan-Turkmenistan/Uzbekistan route. After Taliban took over Kabul, AI took the longer route via south Pakistan and then Iran-Turkey. In a few months, Air India found a way out by overflying the Hindu Kush.A plane gets lighter as it burns fuel, allowing it to ascend. A wide body taking off from Delhi for Europe or North America is tanked up for the non-stop journey and must overfly the Hindu Kush, where minimum altitude is 30,000 feet. The tallest mountain is 25,289-foot Terich Mir.Air India finalised the Hindu Kush route for the B787 after one-and-a-half months of simulator studies as it could fly at about 35,000 feet. For the heavier B777, it took under four months to finalise procedures for overflying Hindukush and ensure it also maintained 30,000 feet.
Article Summary: India is in talks with China to make the Hotan route in Xinjiang available to its airlines. Hotan plan has been in the works for months, with Air India and IndiGo doing feasibility studies. This is the second time in five years that Air India has found an alternate way around an airspace closure.

Article Title: Supreme Court imposes 10 lakh cost on UP government for illegal NSA detention
Article Text:
Noting that the action was taken against him almost two months after the incident, despite the probe agency claiming to have video footage, the court said, 'It defies reason as to why it took the agency to arrest the detenu 54 days after registration of the first FIR'.

Confessional statement alone can’t be basis for detention: SC

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh govt failed to give a satisfactory answer for keeping an accused in the 2024 Sambhal violence case under preventive detention for a year under the National Security Act, the Supreme Court said on Tuesday and slapped a Rs 10 lakh fine on the state, to be paid to the detenu. It also reminded the state to "remain faithful" to the preventive detention jurisprudence and not use it as a punitive measure.Declaring the preventive detention, which was resorted to by the state to keep accused Mulla Afroz in custody after he was granted bail, as illegal, a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said there were multiple flaws in the decision, as evidence to justify it was insufficient. Mulla's confession before police could not have been the sole ground to invoke preventive detention, as in this case, it said.The reliance placed upon the very same occurrence and substantially the same material for sustaining both criminal and preventive detention proceedings lends considerable force to the contention that the detention order has assumed a character more punitive than preventive. We are, therefore, constrained to observe that the state must remain faithful to the rationale underlying preventive detention jurisprudence," the bench said.The detention order was passed on Oct 13 last year. Granting relief to Mulla, SC said, "The appellant has already suffered considerable loss of liberty, even while being granted bail in all cases related to the incident, in which he featured as an accused. In such circumstances, the process was made a punishment."Noting that the action was taken against him almost two months after the incident, despite the probe agency claiming to have video footage, the court said, “It defies reason as to why it took the agency 54 days to arrest the detenu after registration of the first FIR”.“However, the CCTV footage and video recordings, which appear to constitute the sheet-anchor of the allegation, do not find place among the 22 documents relied upon by the detaining authority. Neither have such recordings been furnished to the appellant nor have they been produced before HC or even before us,” it said. The court said an accused person enjoys the fundamental right against self-incrimination and cannot be compelled to be a witness against himself.“We are of the opinion that a confessional statement made before a police officer cannot, by itself, and in absence of any independent material lending support thereto, constitute a basis for forming the subjective satisfaction necessary to sustain an order of preventive detention,” it said. SC added that to permit this would allow a detention order to rest upon a foundation which the law itself excludes from evidentiary consideration.
Article Summary: Supreme Court slapped a Rs 10 lakh fine on the state, to be paid to the detenu. It also reminded the state to "remain faithful" to the preventive detention jurisprudence and not use it as a punitive measure. The detention order was passed on Oct 13 last year.

Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The vesting of assets is the single-most contentious provision in the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill but the law ministry on Tuesday said the proposal was, in fact, an improvement upon the existing law as its ­structured framework enhanced legal certainty, administrative efficiency and accountability in managing foreign-funded assets.The current law provides for vesting of assets but does not specify the nature, duration and finality of such vesting, the ministry told a joint committee of Parliament, which is examining the bill, adding that it led to an open-ended custodial arrangement and administrative difficulties in managing assets, sources said.The ministry was represented by legislative secretary Rajiv Mani at the meeting where State Bank of India, the only bank designated to receive foreign contributions at its New Delhi main branch, supported the bill’s objectives but made a host of suggestions, flagged concerns and sought more clarity, including on how to handle an organisation’s accounts and deposits when its permission to receive foreign donations ends.MPs from opposition parties and BJP clashed over provisions of the bill with two DMK MPs, A Raja and P Wilson, dubbing the bill violative of Article 300(A), which says no one will be deprived of their property save by the ­authority of law.They argued that the Supreme Court has in its rulings explained the ground on which the govt can seize properties and the FCRA bill was violative of this. BJP MP Nishikant Dubey said laws overseeing trusts and societies had ­similar provisions for ­seizure of assets.Turning to alleged misuse of foreign money for conversion, he said this allowed a person converted to a minority religion to enjoy twin quota benefits in some cases, which violated the right to equality. A team of senior SBI officials led by its chairperson C S Setty said while the bill provided for govt control of foreign contributions and ­assets in such cases, it left the detailed banking procedure to be prescribed in rules, ­sources said.SBI officers flagged a ­potential gap between the date when a registration ceased and the date the bank was informed. There is no express protection for banks acting in good faith on the instructions of the designated ­authority or the home ­ministry, they said.The bank said it supported a clear legal framework for managing foreign contributions when an organisation’s registration ended. It called for detailed rules, common procedures for banks and prompt updates on registration status before the new provisions take effect.
Article Summary: MPs from opposition parties and BJP clashed over provisions of the bill with two DMK MPs, A Raja and P Wilson, dubbing the bill violative of Article 300(A), which says no one will be deprived of their property save by the ­authority of law.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday upheld a Delhi HC order directing forensic audit of dissipation of shares of Fortis Healthcare Ltd (FHL) and Fortis Healthcare Holdings Pvt Ltd (FHHPL) through 17 banks and financial institutions allegedly to frustrate execution of a decade-old Rs 5,300 crore foreign decree by Daiichi Sankyo against brothers Malvinder and Shivinder Singh.Brushing aside a challenge to the forensic audit order of the HC by senior advocate Shyam Divan, appearing on behalf of Yes Bank and Axis Bank, a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana clarified the forensic audit would not be a roving inquiry against the banks or FIIs but will focus on the transaction of shares of FHL and FHHPL.The bench also chided Daiichi for giving up its plea for forensic audit of the dissipation of shares in the two companies, which was a major window for the banks to argue that HC could not have passed the order for forensic audit when decree holder had given up that plea.Daiichi counsel Arvind Datar told the court that the foreign decree, upheld by SC, had not been implemented for a decade and the plea giving up forensic audit was made due to frustration over the long lapse of time in executing the decree in India.In fact, Delhi HC judge Justice Subramonium Prasad started his Aug 31 judgement quoting an 1872 judgement of Fort William HC (Calcutta HC) which stated “the difficulty of a litigant in India begins when he has obtained a decree”.Delhi HC had said in its judgment, “For the loans taken by the downstream entities of the judgment-debtors (Singh brothers and their companies), shares of FHL held by FHHPL were kept as security. This court needs to ascertain whether these loans were part of a legitimate transaction for the genuine business or were they part of the fraud to dissipate the shareholding of FHHPL in FHL to defeat the decree.”While directing the forensic auditor to identify each dealing in shareholdings aimed at frustrating the decree, Justice Prasad had asked it to examine “the role of banks, and identify the loan facilities secured by FHL shares, the creation and variation of security, maintenance of security margins, operation of contractual top-up obligations, invocation and sale of pledged shares, release of security, and the outstanding liability corresponding to each transaction”.

Article Title: NCERT text spotlights resistance in medieval India history for Class IX
Article Text:
The emphasis on resistance comes with qualifications. Akbar’s later rule is described as relatively inclusive; Sufism receives attention, while Muslim poets Raskhan and Rahim feature among Bhakti contributors. The chapter describes a period of “both conflict and cooperation”.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: NCERT’s new Class IX social science textbook puts those who resisted conquest at the centre of medieval India’s story, recounting, for instance, Queen Naiki Devi’s defeat of Muhammad Ghuri in 1178 near Mount Abu. The account also acknowledges cooperation across faiths, within a wider curricular shift connecting India’s traditions with contemporary governance and lessons in taxation, insurance and entrepreneurship.The new six-chapter Part 2 of “Understanding Society: India and Beyond” covers history, geography, political science and economics. It continues an overhaul of the earlier syllabus in which class IX history opened with the French Revolution, while economics focused on village production, poverty and food security. It follows the National Curriculum Framework for School Education 2023. Its geography chapters cover “Oceans and Life” and “Life on Earth”.“Resistance and Resilience (1000–1700 CE)” foregrounds Maharana Pratap’s resistance, Lachit Borphukan’s victory at Saraighat and Sikh opposition to Mughal persecution. Rani Abbakka Chowta’s resistance to the Portuguese extends the account beyond confrontations with Muslim rulers.It examines temple destruction and restoration, alongside the role of trade and Bhakti traditions in sustaining communities.The emphasis on resistance comes with qualifications. Akbar’s later rule is described as relatively inclusive; Sufism receives attention, while Muslim poets Raskhan and Rahim feature among Bhakti contributors. The chapter describes a period of “both conflict and cooperation”.Governance lessons invoke Mahatma Gandhi’s conception of Ram Rajya, the Sengol’s Chola associations and the ancient sources of institutional mottos. NEP 2020 is called “an excellent example” of policymaking through consultation, expert advice and public participation. The chapter also addresses misuse of public office and unequal access to services. Khelo Bharat Niti 2025 illustrates coordination between the govts, institutions and the citizens. Students are encouraged to consider their own role in governance, including providing feedback and holding public authorities accountable.Economics becomes more directly practical: students work through income-tax slabs, examine borrowing and investment risks and learn business planning. Ayushman Bharat illustrates health insurance, while entrepreneurship is linked to Viksit Bharat 2047. Lijjat Papad and hotelier Mohan Singh Oberoi provide business case studies. Exercises ask students to examine household budgets, research tax-return filing and prepare their own business plans.Paying taxes is presented as a civic responsibility.The book’s introduction explicitly records two changes to the earlier plan — “Governance and Public Policy” replaces “Authority”, while “India and the World-I” moves to Class X. NCERT says these adjustments make learning “more coherent, age-appropriate and connected”.
Article Summary: NCERT's new Class IX social science textbook puts those who resisted conquest at the centre of medieval India’s story. The account also acknowledges cooperation across faiths, within a wider curricular shift. The new six- chapter Part 2 of ‘Understanding Society: India and Beyond’ covers history, geography, political science and economics.

NEW DELHI: Raising the stakes in the ongoing controversy over special intensive revision (SIR) of poll rolls, the Congress Working Committee on Tuesday demanded that PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah resign on moral grounds, accusing them of being orchestrators of 'vote chori' through CEC Gyanesh Kumar. CWC, chaired by party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, also demanded the CEC's resignation, a halt to the SIR process, and restoration of over 13 crore voters deleted from the rolls.The meeting saw LoP Rahul Gandhi take the lead in arguing that the country now believes what the party and he had been saying for over two years: that the electoral rolls and EVMs were compromised by EC. He lamented that there were "non-believers" in Congress even when evidence was given about "vote chori".Referring to a meeting involving him, PM Modi and Shah, Rahul said the PM told him that after they lose, the Congress government will come in. Rahul had questioned how some appointments were being made despite his opposition, to which the PM had said Indira Gandhi also did that.Rahul said he had replied that Indira was voted out, after which PM Modi made the remark that Congress would follow BJP to office. Sources described the remark's context as Rahul's bid to rally non-believers within by mentioning that even the "BJP mascot" believes Congress will come to office.Rahul is learnt to have said the "big fishes" (PM Modi and Shah) know they are going to lose in future. He said that while there are questions about the 2014 and 2019 elections, the 2024 LS polls were unambiguously "match-fixed", and termed PM Modi as the "illegal PM". He repeatedly stressed "resistance" against the government.Putting Rahul's imprimatur on exposing "vote chori", the CWC resolution, read to the media by KC Venugopal and Jairam Ramesh, noted, "what began as one man's solitary warning is now a national demand for transparency and accountability".CWC stopped short of deciding an action plan, leaving it to the INDIA bloc, which will meet Wednesday.CWC meeting was attended by Sonia Gandhi, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Sachin Pilot, Shashi Tharoor, Abhishek Singhvi, Manish Tewari, Randeep Singh Surjewala, Jitendra Singh, Prakash Joshi, CMs DK Shivakumar, Sukhwinder Sukhu, VD Satheesan, and Revanth Reddy, among others. Many CWC members and the four CMs are learnt to have argued that agitation in Delhi is important to having an impact.Kharge said, "Like in British times, Congress again has to shoulder the responsibility... we snatched the right to vote from the British and now fight to save that right."When Tharoor said the party should support the CJP agitation called on Oct 2, Kharge caustically asked the Keralam MP if he would be seen only in newspapers and on TV, or would join the street battle against the EC.
Article Summary: The Congress Working Committee on Tuesday demanded that PM Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah resign on moral grounds. CWC, chaired by party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, also demanded the CEC's resignation, a halt to the SIR process, and restoration of over 13 crore voters deleted from the rolls.

Article Title: ‘Court must protect liberty of accused if trial may be delayed’, says Supreme Court
Article Text:
The accused were arrested for their alleged involvement in massive financial irregularities in the execution of ‘Jal Jeevan Mission’, an ambitious joint initiative of the central and state govts intended to provide functional household tap connections for safe and adequate drinking water supply.

Accused were held for ‘jal mission’ irregularities

NEW DELHI: Observing that the right to personal liberty of the accused becomes paramount if trial is unlikely to be completed in the near future, the Supreme Court has said bail must be granted in such cases.“It is a well-settled postulate of criminal jurisprudence that pre-trial incarceration cannot masquerade as punitive detention... This court must intervene to safeguard the right to personal liberty under Article 21 of the Constitution... when a trial cannot be reasonably concluded in the near future,” a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and Sheel Nagu said.The bench granted bail to ex-secretary of Rajasthan Water Supply and Sewerage Management Board Shubhanshu Dixit, who has been in custody since Feb 17, when he was arrested in a graft case.The court also granted relief to a person who was allegedly operating as a broker on behalf of the then cabinet minister of the Public Health Engineering Department, Rajasthan, Mahesh Chandra Joshi.The accused were arrested for their alleged involvement in massive financial irregularities in the execution of ‘Jal Jeevan Mission’, an ambitious joint initiative of the central and state govts intended to provide functional household tap connections for safe and adequate drinking water supply.Though the court accepted the plea of state govt that economic offences involving deep-rooted conspiracies must be viewed seriously, it granted relief to the accused.“Admittedly, the charges are yet to be framed and the trial is yet to commence for, inter alia, the following reasons: the investigation against some of the accused persons is still pending; two of the accused persons are absconding; and sanction under Section 19 of the PoC Act was granted on Sept 6 for the prosecution of six other co-accused persons who are public servants. Bearing in mind the sheer volume of evidence that must be led to prove the charges, the trial is bound to be a protracted exercise. In the conspectus of these aspects, we are of the view that it would serve no fruitful purpose to keep the appellants under further pre-trial custody. Resultantly, the present appeals succeed,” the court said.
Article Summary: The accused were arrested for their alleged involvement in massive financial irregularities in the execution of ‘Jal Jeevan Mission’ The bench granted bail to ex-secretary of Rajasthan Water Supply and Sewerage Management Board Shubhanshu Dixit.

SRINAGAR: A day after the Jammu & Kashmir assembly passed a resolution seeking restoration of statehood with a reference to autonomy, leader of opposition Sunil Sharma said the move would strain Centre-J&K relations and urged chief secretary Atal Dulloo not to forward the resolution to the Union govt. The BJP member also demanded speaker Abdul Rahim Rather’s resignation and claimed that Union home minister Amit Shah was unhappy about the resolution.“Already the chief secretary and the law secretary gave their opinion to the assembly that they cannot discuss the resolution as the issue is sub judice. Their communication to the assembly secretariat ahead of the resolution is an indication that the resolution is anti-Constitution. We expect the chief secretary not to forward the resolution to the Centre and throw it away,” Sharma told TOI.Sources said the assembly secretariat had sent the resolution to the chief secretary to be forwarded to the Centre.NC legislator Justice (retired) Hasnain Masoodi said the assembly secretariat should have directly sent it to the central govt instead of routing it through the chief secretary, as he had objected to the resolution.The assembly Monday adopted the resolution that seeks restoration of statehood amid protests and a walkout by BJP legislators, who accused NC and Congress of being anti-national over the reference to the autonomy resolution passed in the House in 2000.The chief secretary and the law secretary are facing criticism from the National Conference and other parties for writing to the assembly secretariat earlier, advising against taking up the resolution.Speaking in the House on Monday, CM Omar Abdullah, who moved the resolution, said he was also the law minister and was not even aware “that my law secretary is sending you opinions”.Sharma defended the two bureaucrats, saying they had expressed the “right opinion” as the resolution, he claimed, was “anti-constitutional” and “anti-national”.He said the speaker not only allowed the resolution to be introduced but also permitted amendments referring to autonomy and condemning the abrogation of Article 370, which was upheld by the Supreme Court. “The speaker has to step down,” he added. BJP has already moved a motion in the assembly against Rather.Sharma said the Centre was unhappy over the resolution as it would encourage separatism in J&K. “I met the (Union) home minister (Amit Shah) on Sunday. He expressed displeasure over the resolution,” Sharma said.According to Sharma, Shah told him during the meeting in New Delhi that statehood would be restored to J&K at an “appropriate time”, but anything that could disturb the peaceful situation would not be allowed.

Article Text:
